question.text: Potassium chlorate is prepared by the electrolysis of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KCl</mi></math> in basic solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>OH</mi><mo>-</mo></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>Cl</mi><mo>-</mo></msup><mo>→</mo><msubsup><mi>ClO</mi><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mo>-</mo></msup></math> . If only <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the current is utilized in the reaction, the time (rounded to the nearest hour) required to produce<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>KClO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> using a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></math> (Given :<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>96</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>500</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mol</mi></math>; molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>KClO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>122</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
